content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged Chinese pangolin frame. Host frame: the Chinese pangolin sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines an axolotl and a Chinese pangolin. Head of the Chinese pangolin, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: behavior follows pangolin head/brain donor: nocturnal solitary foraging, stays near water to keep gills moist; body: pangolin torso and scaled frame sets shape as structured host; retains pangolin lungs for air breathing with axolotl gills supplemental; axolotl skin in a few large patches over the back and flanks, at full strength with clean edges, color and surface unchanged inside each patch; Chinese pangolin coat everywhere else; ears: pangolin small reduced ears; face: pangolin narrow snout and mouth for ant and termite feeding; feet: pangolin clawed feet for digging; head: pangolin head shape; axolotl gills attached externally, not blended into skull; limbs: four pangolin legs, no extra limbs; skull: pangolin skull supports feeding; tail: long scaled pangolin tail; plain coat, no stripes or spots. Coat texture flows along the body outline. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (river forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature concept**
I'm planning a four-legged pangolin silhouette with a fully visible pangolin head and clear eyes, adding axolotl skin patches on the back and flanks, supplemental gills near water, and pangolin scales and lungs for the overall structure.
**Finding reference anatomy details**
I'm gathering reference images of a Chinese pangolin and axolotl gills to check scale patterns, head shape, and frilly external gills before drafting the natural history illustration.
**Finding axolotl gill details**
I'm looking up axolotl gill anatomy to gather clear reference details for the user's project.
**Generating hybrid illustration**
I'm creating a natural history illustration of the pangolin-axolotl hybrid, with a three-quarter head view, scaled body, pink axolotl skin patches on the back and flanks, and external gills behind the ears on a plain light background.
**Refining hybrid illustration**
I'm adjusting the gills to sit lower behind the head and switching to a side three-quarter view to make the hybrid look more natural, then generating one more version.
